study_material.title: Character Puzzle - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: Character puzzles show a grid, triangle or wheel of numbers/letters with one missing, and ask you to find it from the hidden rule. The rules are arithmetic on rows, columns, diagonals or around a centre.
learning_objectives: Test row-wise, column-wise and diagonal rules systematically
Handle letter grids via alphabet positions
Verify a candidate rule on every complete row before applying

concepts.heading: 1. Row and Column Rules
concepts.body: Try: third = first op second (add, subtract, multiply, divide); third = combination like a x b - c. Example rows (2, 3, 6), (4, 5, 20): third = product. Apply the confirmed rule to the incomplete row.

concepts.heading: 2. Centre Rules
concepts.body: In figures with a centre cell: centre = sum, product or difference of outer values, sometimes divided by a constant. Example: corners 3, 4, 5 with centre 12 = sum; next figure 6, 7, 8 gives centre 21.

concepts.heading: 3. Power Patterns
concepts.body: Squares and cubes hide in pairs: (5, 25), (7, 49), (9, 81). Sequences like 8, 27, 64 are consecutive cubes. When numbers grow fast, test powers before products.

concepts.heading: 4. Letter Grids
concepts.body: Convert letters to positions (A=1..Z=26) and hunt the same arithmetic rules. Rules may run clockwise around a wheel - check both directions.

concepts.heading: 5. Verification Discipline
concepts.body: A rule must fit EVERY complete row/figure, not just one. If two rules fit, prefer the simpler; placement answers are single-step arithmetic far more often than exotic combinations.

formulas: Test op order: +, -, x, /, then powers
shortcut_methods: Confirm the rule on all given rows before computing the answer
Check both clockwise and anticlockwise on wheels
common_mistakes: Fitting a rule to only one row
Ignoring position order (a op b vs b op a)
Missing that the rule may involve all three cells, not two
study_material.summary: Enumerate simple arithmetic rules, verify on every complete figure, then fill the blank.
quick_revision_notes: Rows first, then columns, then diagonals
Centre often = sum or product of outer

solved_examples.question: Rows: (2, 3, 6), (4, 5, 20), (6, 7, ?). Find the missing number.
solved_examples.step_by_step: Third = product of first two: 6 x 7 = 42.
solved_examples.shortcut: Check the rule on both complete rows first.

practice_questions.explanation: Second letter = first + 2 positions: J(10) + 2 = L(12).
